pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Guess what! gets attention before a story.
You won’t believe it means it is a very small thing.
A story in the past uses the simple past.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Guess what! gets attention before a story. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
You won’t believe it means it is a very small thing. → Falso (It means it is surprising.)
A story in the past uses the simple past. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A funny story · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy morning in a small café in Portland. The smell of fresh coffee fills the air. Leo sits by the window with his phone. He cannot stop smiling. His friend Ada comes in and sees him. She asks what he is laughing at.
“Leo, you are laughing alone! What is so funny?” says Ada. “Guess what! A funny thing happened on the bus today.” says Leo. “Tell me! I love a good story.” says Ada.
